verdict.rationale: ByteAsk is documented as a C/C++ coding agent that edits repository files, compiles, runs your test suite, and presents a diff for review. That gives general code-modification capability that could cover these chores, but none of the four named tasks is specifically documented. missing for 10: explicit test-writing capability, lint-error fixing, merge-conflict resolution, dependency updating, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the agent write tests, fix lint errors, resolve merge conflicts, and update dependencies for me

citations.quote: ByteAsk opens a full-screen TUI, reads your codebase, edits files, compiles, runs tests, and presents a diff for your review before making permanent changes
It edits your repository from the terminal, then drives the real toolchain - sanitizers, your test suite, and any gdb session you already have open - and hands you a diff that survived the debugger.
If you want the agent to build, test, or write files, pass `--sandbox workspace-write`.
